subject: Mean Differences of Latent Variables across Multiple Groups

messages.author: 22e446caca9e58a5
messages.subject: Mean Differences of Latent Variables across Multiple Groups
parts:
Hi! I was wondering how to deal with mean differences among latent variables. For example, I have two models below. They are very different (multiple groups vs. single group, huge difference in the number of parameters to estimate). model1 doesn't have good fit, however, model2 has an acceptable fit. 

> model1<-'
        LV1 =~ item_1+item_2+item_3+item_4
        LV2 =~ item_5+item_6+item_7
        LV3 =~ item_8+item_9+item_10
        LV1 ~~ LV2
        LV2 ~~ LV3
        LV1 ~~ LV3
'
> cfa(model1, data=data, group="myGroups",
         group.equal =c("loadings","intercepts","lv.variances", "residual.covariances","residuals"), meanstructure=T)

> model2<-'
        LV1 =~ item_1+item_2+item_3+item_4
        LV2 =~ item_5+item_6+item_7
        LV3 =~ item_8+item_9+item_10
        LV1 ~~ LV2
        LV2 ~~ LV3
        LV1 ~~ LV3
        LV1 ~ grp2 + grp3 + grp4
        LV2 ~ grp2 + grp3 + grp4
        LV3 ~ grp2 + grp3 + grp4
' # grp2-grp4 are dummies.
> sem(model2, data=data)

My questions are:
1. If I assume there are groups in the sample, is the multiple group approach a more appropriate way to start? 
2. Since model2 fit is good, can I report model2 as a way to compare mean differences across the four groups (grp1-grp4, using grp1 as reference)? If I report it, can I interpret it as the way we interpret in multiple regression?

Thank you for your help!!!

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: Mean Differences of Latent Variables across Multiple Groups
parts:
1. Certainly. If your theoretical framework includes multiple groups, why would you do anything else (apart from a MIMIC model in special constellations, invariance and the question of sample size).
2. sem(model2, data=data) does not compute a multi-group model. What exactly do you want to do?

Well, if model1 does not fit well and model2 is acceptable, then there is some probability that invariance is not present. I would first check this and not use model2 regardless of the statements you interpret into it, because in my opinion you are simply masking a potential problem.
